## Install everything from one place

Add the claudemods marketplace once, then install any mod by name:

```
/plugin marketplace add omarcevi/claudemods
/plugin install cc-arcade@claudemods
```

Every plugin in the marketplace points at the exact upstream commit we looked at, so a mod can't change under you until we review and bump it.

> [!WARNING]
> Mods and plugins run with **your** permissions. They can read files, run commands and use the network. Read a mod's source before you install it.

### Writing styles

Change how Claude writes answers and commit messages.

| Name | What it does | Install |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [caveman-mode](https://github.com/baselane-sh/mods/tree/main/plugins/caveman-mode)<br><sub>by mohammad0omar</sub> | Prose in short caveman speech ("Fix bug. Test pass."), still accurate. Code and commands stay exact. | `/plugin install caveman-mode@claudemods` |
| [code-only](https://github.com/baselane-sh/mods/tree/main/plugins/code-only)<br><sub>by mohammad0omar</sub> | Replies with the code or command first and at most two short sentences of prose, unless asked to explain. | `/plugin install code-only@claudemods` |
| [conventional-commits](https://github.com/baselane-sh/mods/tree/main/plugins/conventional-commits)<br><sub>by mohammad0omar</sub> | Commit messages follow Conventional Commits: type(scope): subject, imperative, under 72 characters. | `/plugin install conventional-commits@claudemods` |
| [eli5-mode](https://github.com/baselane-sh/mods/tree/main/plugins/eli5-mode)<br><sub>by mohammad0omar</sub> | Explains like the reader is new: analogies first, no jargon without a one-line definition. | `/plugin install eli5-mode@claudemods` |
| [gitmoji-commits](https://github.com/baselane-sh/mods/tree/main/plugins/gitmoji-commits)<br><sub>by mohammad0omar</sub> | Commit messages start with the matching gitmoji (✨ feat, 🐛 fix). Composes with conventional-commits: emoji goes before the type. | `/plugin install gitmoji-commits@claudemods` |
| [junior-mode](https://github.com/baselane-sh/mods/tree/main/plugins/junior-mode)<br><sub>by mohammad0omar</sub> | Explains each step and why, and defines jargon once, for a learner. | `/plugin install junior-mode@claudemods` |
| [no-em-dash](https://github.com/baselane-sh/mods/tree/main/plugins/no-em-dash)<br><sub>by mohammad0omar</sub> | Never writes the em-dash character. Uses a comma, colon, period or parentheses. | `/plugin install no-em-dash@claudemods` |
| [no-sycophancy](https://github.com/baselane-sh/mods/tree/main/plugins/no-sycophancy)<br><sub>by mohammad0omar</sub> | No flattery or filler. Disagreement is stated plainly, with the reason. | `/plugin install no-sycophancy@claudemods` |
| [pirate-mode](https://github.com/baselane-sh/mods/tree/main/plugins/pirate-mode)<br><sub>by mohammad0omar</sub> | Talks like a pirate in prose, never inside code, commands or file contents. | `/plugin install pirate-mode@claudemods` |
| [plain-english](https://github.com/baselane-sh/mods/tree/main/plugins/plain-english)<br><sub>by mohammad0omar</sub> | Writes in ASD-STE-100 Simplified Technical English: short sentences, active voice, simple words. | `/plugin install plain-english@claudemods` |
| [reply-language](https://github.com/baselane-sh/mods/tree/main/plugins/reply-language)<br><sub>by mohammad0omar</sub> | Answers in the language you set (English by default). Code, identifiers and commands stay as they are. | `/plugin install reply-language@claudemods` |
| [security-mode](https://github.com/baselane-sh/mods/tree/main/plugins/security-mode)<br><sub>by mohammad0omar</sub> | Checks each change for injection, secrets, authorization and unsafe input, and states the risks it checked. | `/plugin install security-mode@claudemods` |
| [shakespeare-mode](https://github.com/baselane-sh/mods/tree/main/plugins/shakespeare-mode)<br><sub>by mohammad0omar</sub> | Prose in Early Modern English flair. Code, commands, commit messages and error text stay exact. | `/plugin install shakespeare-mode@claudemods` |
| [ste-mode](https://github.com/baselane-sh/mods/tree/main/plugins/ste-mode)<br><sub>by mohammad0omar</sub> | Replies in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English: approved words, short sentences, one instruction each, active voice. | `/plugin install ste-mode@claudemods` |

| [Claude Plugins Official](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official) ⭐<br><sub>by anthropics</sub> | Anthropic-managed directory of curated Claude Code plugins from Anthropic and partners. | `/plugin install <plugin>@claude-plugins-official` |
| [claude-mem](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem) ⭐<br><sub>by thedotmack</sub> | Records what your agent does, compresses it, and feeds relevant context back into future sessions. | `/plugin install agent-mem@claudemods`<br>`/plugin install agent-mem-cowork@claudemods` |

| [Claude Code bundled plugins](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code)<br><sub>by anthropics</sub> | Anthropic's own plugins: code review, commit commands, feature dev, hookify, plugin-dev and more. | `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-code` |

## Skills

## How it works

- `data/mods.json` is the only file people edit. One entry per mod, plugin, skill or link.
- `scripts/sync.mjs` reads each `bundle: true` entry's upstream `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (or `plugin.json`), pins it to the current commit and saves the result in `data/resolved.json`.
- `scripts/build.mjs` generates this README, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and the site.
- `scripts/footprint.mjs` reads every bundled plugin at its pinned commit and records what it runs: shell hooks, function-hook modules and the `$` calls they make, MCP servers, plus flags such as network access, running programs, touching credentials or skipping permission prompts. The site shows it on every card. A plugin that fetches code at runtime isn't bundled unless its entry says why (`acknowledge`).
- A weekly GitHub Action re-syncs and opens a pull request with any new commits and what changed in what each plugin runs, so every upstream change gets a human look before it reaches you. Another installs every plugin into a clean config each week.

## Contributing

The easiest way is the [submission form](https://github.com/omarcevi/claudemods/issues/new?template=submit.yml). A maintainer reviews it, labels it `approved`, and a bot opens the pull request for you. You can also edit `data/mods.json` directly; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).
